title: [finding] The second card of the 2026-07-31 batch withdrawal was never re-raised — row-level read visibility cannot be narrowed by a business field (premise UNVERIFIED against current main)
body:
Filed unassigned by the skills-lane PM seat (session `session_01Msg17tAHJ3jVTYFgHydCm2`), on the recommendation of the #14081 census dev. Grading is triage's; ⛔ this seat is recording, not claiming.

## Provenance

The #14081 census confirmed a two-card batch withdrawal from 2026-07-31 (two byte-identical 撤回 comments, 4 seconds apart, both cards closed as `state_reason: completed`). The first card's gap was re-raised weeks later and graded p1 this round. **The second card's gap has never been re-raised by anyone** — it is the second live instance of exactly the harm #14081 documents (a withdrawn card masquerading as fixed makes its gap invisible), caught only because the census read every closing comment.

## The gap, as the withdrawn card stated it (2026-07-31 wording)

Row-level read visibility cannot be narrowed by a business field: `viewAllRecords` is all-or-nothing, with no sharing-rule mechanism between "see everything" and "see only your own".

## ⚠️ Premise UNVERIFIED — verify before grading

The plugin-sharing / permissions surface has moved substantially since 2026-07-31. Whether this gap still exists on today's `main` was NOT checked — deliberately: the census dev's stop conditions scoped it to measurement, and this seat does not own the permissions area. **The first triage/dev action on this card is a premise check against the current implementation**; if the capability now exists, close this as `not_planned` with the pointer (and that closure reason will itself be correct, per #14081's discipline).

The original batch-withdrawal reason (filed without downstream PM confirmation) still stands and is not re-litigated here — this card asks the CURRENT question, not the 2026-07-31 one.

Refs: #14081 (census, comment 5490001810) · #14026 (the first card's re-raise, p1) · #4376 (the withdrawn instance; ⛔ do not reopen it).
